releases.headline: Restores auto-rollback for the full-size binaries, adds a cooperative Windows daemon stop, and hardens sync recovery
releases.summary: This release refreshes the vendored security framework and fixes several correctness and robustness issues across the auto-update, daemon, file-watch, and sync-reconcile paths. Auto-update rollback now works for the full-size platform binaries on Linux and macOS, Windows `stop` performs a cooperative graceful shutdown instead of a forced terminate, and secrets embedded in log messages are masked before they reach the log file. No configuration changes are required.

items.title: Auto-update rollback restored for the full-size binaries on Linux and macOS
items.body: A failed auto-update could not automatically roll back to the previous binary on Linux or macOS: the restore step refused any backup larger than 64 MiB, and the platform binaries exceed that size, so a build that failed its post-install probation stayed installed with no automatic recovery. The restore now handles the full binary size, so a bad update is reverted to the prior working binary as intended. It also now confirms the on-disk binary is still the probationary build before restoring, so a binary replaced by another mechanism is left in place.

items.title: Windows stop performs a graceful shutdown
items.body: On Windows, `hermitstash-sync stop` previously waited out a timeout and then forcibly terminated the daemon, cutting any in-flight upload and skipping the orderly state-database close. It now signals the running daemon to drain and shut down cleanly — the same teardown performed on other platforms — and only escalates to a forced stop if the daemon does not respond in time.

items.title: File watcher recovers from a native handle failure
items.body: If the operating system file-change backend died (for example on inotify exhaustion, or when the watched folder was removed and recreated), the watcher treated the failure as transient and never restarted, silently leaving local changes undetected until the daemon was restarted. It now recognizes a dead handle and re-creates the watcher automatically.

items.title: Windows ignore rules written with backslashes now prune folders
items.body: A subtree ignore pattern written with Windows path separators (for example `data\cache\**`) was not applied when skipping folders during the periodic scan, so a large ignored subtree could still be walked. Such patterns are now normalized and pruned correctly.

items.title: A failed server change event is re-delivered after reconnect instead of being skipped
items.body: If applying a change event from the server failed (for example a transient local-database error), a later successful event could advance the sync position past the failed one, so the server would not re-send it on the next reconnect and the change could be missed. A failed event now holds the sync position so the reconnect re-delivers it.

items.title: The periodic reconcile no longer races a live transfer
items.body: The background reconcile that re-drives stranded transfers could act on a file that a live download or upload was already handling, occasionally producing a spurious conflict copy or a transient mismatch. The reconcile now skips any path a live transfer owns and is serialized against live server events.

items.title: Upload metrics stay live after an internal engine restart
items.body: The upload queue-depth and in-flight gauges could freeze after the sync engine restarted itself following a failed auto-update install. They are now re-registered on restart so telemetry stays accurate.

items.title: Secrets embedded in a log message are masked before they reach disk
items.body: A credential interpolated into the middle of a log message — a token, an API key, a URL with an embedded password — could reach the log file and console unmasked. Log messages are now scrubbed with word-boundary matching so an embedded secret is redacted while the surrounding message stays readable, and the support-diagnostic bundle applies the same scrubbing to older log lines.

items.title: The status and stats commands no longer alter daemon state
items.body: The `status` and `stats` commands — commonly used as container and service health probes — could remove a stale PID file as a side effect, which could then make a following `stop` report that no daemon was running. They are now read-only and never modify the PID file.

items.title: Vendored security framework updated to blamejs v0.17.23
items.body: The vendored blamejs framework is updated from v0.17.11 to v0.17.23, bringing its latest post-quantum TLS, redaction, self-update, file-watch, and daemon hardening plus a refreshed public-suffix list for domain classification. Several client components now consume its shared primitives directly (the TLS certificate-pin derivation, the loopback-host classification for the plaintext-transport gate, the free-text log redactor, and the file-watch ignore caps), reducing duplicated security-relevant code.

releases.headline: Publishes the container image for the v0.10.6 fixes
releases.summary: A maintenance release. The v0.10.6 platform binaries carried a large batch of sync-correctness and hardening fixes but its container image did not publish; v0.10.7 carries the identical fixes and provides the multi-architecture container image. The only source change from v0.10.6 is a development-time lint adjustment that is not part of the shipped binary, so the v0.10.6 and v0.10.7 binaries are functionally equivalent. No configuration changes are required. See the v0.10.6 notes for the full list of fixes.

items.title: Container image available for the v0.10.6 fix set
items.body: The container image at ghcr.io/dotcoocoo/hermitstash-sync is published for this release, carrying the same sync-correctness, data-loss, and security fixes shipped in the v0.10.6 platform binaries. Operators on the pre-built binaries are already covered by v0.10.6; container users should pull this release.

releases.headline: Restores background-daemon mode in the pre-built binaries and fixes a broad set of sync data-loss and recovery edge cases
releases.summary: A correctness and hardening release. It restores `start --daemon` in the pre-built binaries (it silently never started a daemon while reporting success), refuses to enroll over plaintext HTTP so an API key and mTLS private key can no longer leak, and closes a broad set of rare but real sync-engine edge cases that could drop a delete, revert or destroy an un-uploaded edit, delete a just-recreated file, leak a file on the server, or wedge the client in a permanent catching-up state. Nested build and repository directories (a project checked out inside the synced folder) are now correctly ignored. No configuration changes are required.

items.title: `start --daemon` works again in the pre-built binaries
items.body: In the released single-file binaries the background daemon never actually started — the parent printed "Daemon started" and exited while the detached worker died immediately parsing its own path as a command, leaving a stale PID file and no syncing. It now starts correctly on every platform, and a worker that dies during startup is reported instead of masked as success. Running from source was unaffected.

items.title: A failed auto-update install resumes syncing instead of going idle
items.body: If an update download verified but the install step failed (for example an anti-virus scanner holding the binary open on Windows), the daemon stopped its sync engine for the swap and then, on failure, left it stopped — syncing silently ceased until the process was restarted. A failed install now restarts the sync engine (re-reading any live pattern changes) and continues on the running version, and the auto-update recovery path was hardened against several rare states that could roll a healthy update back or strand a partially-installed one.

items.title: A delete is no longer silently undone by a single failed server request
items.body: When a local delete's server request failed once (a transient network blip), the file was later re-downloaded by the recovery pass and reappeared on every device — the delete was dropped. A failed delete is now retried on its own rather than being mistaken for a failed download, and a delete for content the client never actually held (a download that never landed) is no longer propagated to the server.

items.title: An un-uploaded local edit is preserved across a rename
items.body: Renaming a file whose most recent edit had not yet reached the server (a failed or in-flight upload) could mark it as fully synced under the new name — so the edit was never sent — or, when the rename coincided with a remote change, overwrite the edit outright. The renamed file now keeps its pending upload so the edit is sent, and a colliding remote change preserves the local edit as a conflict copy.

items.title: Deleting then quickly recreating a file no longer deletes the new file
items.body: Recreating a file within a second of deleting it (common with tool-regenerated output) could let the buffered delete fire after the recreate's upload and remove the new file from the server. A same-path recreate now supersedes the pending delete, and the delete step additionally skips any path whose file has reappeared.

items.title: Deleting a file mid-upload no longer leaks it on the server
items.body: Deleting a brand-new file while its first upload was still in flight left the file on the server forever and a permanent stuck record locally. The vanished file is now recognized as a delete and removed from the server.

items.title: The client no longer gets stuck in a permanent catching-up state
items.body: After an event that could not be applied at the moment (a momentarily locked file), the change cursor could freeze for the rest of the session — the client reported catching-up indefinitely and its last-sync time went stale even though data was flowing. The cursor now clears once the delayed event finally applies, and a failed case-only rename no longer lets a later event skip past it.

items.title: A temporarily-unreadable synced folder no longer deletes everything
items.body: If the synced folder itself became briefly unreadable — an unmounted network or removable volume — every tracked file looked deleted and those deletes could propagate to the server and every device. Local deletes are now ignored while the synced folder is unreadable and reconsidered once it returns.

items.title: A project checked out inside the synced folder is correctly ignored
items.body: The default ignores for repository and build directories (.git, node_modules, __pycache__, and similar) only applied at the top of the synced folder, so a project cloned into a subfolder uploaded its entire .git and node_modules trees. These directories are now ignored at any depth. Ignore and include patterns also now accept a Windows-style backslash separator and match regardless of Unicode composition.

items.title: Smaller correctness fixes
items.body: A crash-interrupted upload is now actually re-sent by the recovery pass rather than silently skipped; shutdown waits for in-flight downloads before closing so it no longer logs spurious errors; a manually-entered API key is trimmed and an empty one refused; the credential file is read without a race that could report a spurious error during a concurrent re-enrollment; and a routine save-then-delete during hashing no longer logs at error level.

items.title: Enrollment refuses plaintext HTTP to a non-loopback server
items.body: The enrollment exchange sends your enrollment code and receives your API key and mTLS private key. Over plaintext http:// to a non-loopback host these travelled in the clear, and the existing refusal only ran later when the daemon started — after the credentials had already been exposed. Enrollment now refuses a non-loopback http:// server before sending anything. A loopback address (a TLS-terminating sidecar) is still allowed, and HERMITSTASH_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=1 remains the explicit opt-out.

items.title: Lookups keyed on untrusted names reject inherited object members
items.body: Several internal lookups (log level, license identifier, changelog heading, configuration keys) resolved a name against a table without an own-property check, so a name matching a built-in object member could slip a validation. All now use own-property checks. A support-bundle credential scrub also matches the authorization scheme case-insensitively, and an in-string bearer-token detector now redacts a credential embedded in a log message in the live log and on standard output, not only in the support bundle.

items.title: Adopted newly hardened framework primitives
items.body: The auto-update signature verifier, the metrics exposition renderer, the post-quantum TLS agent's group configuration (now validated), release-time version ordering, and several internal reads now route through the vendored framework's hardened primitives instead of local re-implementations, and the loopback-host and certificate-pin derivations are consolidated to single implementations. No behavior visible to operators changes.

items.title: Vendored framework advanced to blamejs v0.17.11
items.body: Carries upstream security and correctness fixes across the wire, crypto, and process layers, including a DER decoder that rejects a non-minimal length encoding (closing a parser differential under every certificate parse), a WebSocket client that connects to wss:// hosts given as IP literals, a shared HTTP cache that no longer serves an authenticated response across principals, safe-decompression that refuses an unknown algorithm instead of returning input unchanged, and a family of lookup guards that reject prototype-member names.

items.title: Refreshed the pinned GitHub Actions
items.body: The commit-pinned actions in the release and container-publish workflows were advanced to their current releases (still pinned by commit hash with a version comment).

releases.headline: Stops spurious conflict copies on multi-device edits and fixes several sync-recovery and lifecycle edge cases
releases.summary: A correctness release. It stops the client from creating (and fanning out) a spurious conflict copy when another device edits a shared file — the single most common multi-device operation — closes a rare case where a locked local file during catch-up could let a server-side delete be missed, keeps a certificate renewal from aborting an in-progress transfer, ensures a background daemon's final error line reaches its log file, and makes enrollment fail clearly when the server returns no API key. No configuration changes are required.

items.title: Editing a shared file on another device no longer creates a spurious conflict copy
items.body: When another device changed a file and the server broadcast the replacement, a receiving device that still held the previous synced version incorrectly treated it as a local divergence — writing a .conflict copy of the already-synced content and then, because that copy looks like a new local file, uploading it so the junk propagated to every device. The client now recognizes the un-diverged previous version and skips the conflict copy; a genuine local edit made before the remote change is still preserved as a conflict copy exactly as before.

items.title: A locked local file during catch-up no longer lets a server-side delete be missed
items.body: If a remote delete arrived for a file the client could not read at that moment (locked or unreadable), it correctly kept the file and left the change for a later retry — but a subsequent catch-up reconnect could advance the change cursor past the un-applied delete, so it was never re-delivered and the file lingered with a stale record. The catch-up recovery now refuses to advance past an event that failed to apply, leaving a visible, self-healing stall until the file is readable again.

items.title: A certificate renewal no longer aborts an in-progress transfer
items.body: When the client rotated its mTLS credentials (on renewal or a CA rotation) it replaced its connection pool and destroyed the previous pool on a fixed 30-second timer — which could cut off a large upload or download still running on an existing connection. The previous pool is now closed only once its in-flight transfers finish (bounded by the existing per-transfer ceiling), so a healthy transfer completes across a credential rotation.

items.title: A background daemon's final error line now reaches its log file
items.body: When the daemon exited on a fatal startup or authentication error, it wrote the final diagnostic and terminated before the asynchronous file logger had flushed, so that last line was lost from the rotated log — a daemon's primary post-mortem record. Those exit paths now flush the log (bounded) before exiting.

items.title: Enrollment fails clearly when the server returns no API key
items.body: The interactive and headless enrollment flows assumed a successful response always carried an API key. A success response without one (for example a certificate-reissue code sent to the enrollment path) is now rejected with a message that points to the repair command, instead of storing an empty credential and failing opaquely later.

releases.headline: Hardens the container build and the systemd / Podman / Kubernetes / Unraid deployment paths
releases.summary: A deployment-surface release. It digest-pins the container build's verify stage (closing a path where a republished base tag could ship a backdoored signed binary), fixes the systemd auto-updater so it actually rolls back when a new binary won't start, stops the installer from overwriting an operator-edited update config, and tightens the Kubernetes and Unraid references. The client binary and its behavior are unchanged; these are build- and deploy-layer fixes.

items.title: The container build's verify stage is digest-pinned
items.body: The two-stage image build runs the SHA3-512 + ECDSA signature check — and materializes the binary copied into the runtime image — in a first stage based on node:24.18.0-slim. That base was a mutable tag while the runtime base was already digest-pinned, so a republished base tag could have run attacker code in the verify stage and shipped a backdoored binary that then carried a valid cosign signature and SLSA attestation. The verify-stage base is now pinned to an immutable digest, on the same refresh cadence as the runtime base.

items.title: The systemd auto-updater rolls back when a new binary won't start
items.body: The external updater (deploy/update.sh) restarts the service after swapping in a new binary, then health-checks it. Under `set -e`, a restart that returned non-zero — exactly what happens when the new binary crash-loops or never signals ready — aborted the script before the rollback ran, leaving the broken binary installed and the daemon down. The restart no longer aborts the script; the health probe decides, and an unhealthy start now rolls back to the previous binary as intended.

items.title: Reinstalling no longer overwrites your updater configuration
items.body: Re-running deploy/install.sh reset /etc/default/hermitstash-sync-update to the shipped all-commented default, silently discarding an operator edit such as a paused auto-update. The installer now writes that file only when it is absent; on an upgrade it drops the shipped template beside it as a .new file to diff, leaving your configuration intact.

items.title: The installer prints an actionable hint when it can't resolve the latest release
items.body: If the GitHub API call that resolves the latest version failed (for example an unauthenticated rate-limit), `set -e` aborted the installer before its 'set VERSION=X.Y.Z to pin' guidance could print. The resolve step no longer aborts, so the actionable message is shown.

items.title: The Podman runner waits for first-run enrollment before handing off
items.body: On first run, deploy/podman.sh enrolled inside a bootstrap container and then replaced it with a Quadlet unit that carries no enrollment code. If enrollment hadn't finished writing its config to the volume in that window, the Quadlet container crash-looped as unconfigured. The runner now waits (bounded) for the config to be persisted — or for a failed enrollment to surface — before the hand-off.

items.title: Uninstall removes a leftover in-progress update binary
items.body: deploy/uninstall.sh removed the installed binary and its rollback copy but not a `.new` staging file left by an update interrupted mid-swap. That file is now swept as well, and the updater clears a stale `.new` on exit.

items.title: Kubernetes manifest drops the service-account token and re-pulls a rebuilt image
items.body: The reference Deployment is outbound-only and never calls the Kubernetes API, so it now sets automountServiceAccountToken: false — removing a default credential a compromised client could use for lateral movement. Its imagePullPolicy is now Always (instead of IfNotPresent) so a rebuilt, security-patched :latest is re-pulled on restart; pin the image to a @sha256 digest in your overlay for a reproducible, cosign-verifiable deployment.

items.title: Unraid template drops the ineffective PUID/PGID variables
items.body: The container runs as a fixed non-root user (uid:gid 1000:1000) by design, so the template's PUID/PGID variables were silently ignored. They have been removed; set your appdata and synced host folders to owner 1000:1000 (or group-writable for gid 1000) instead — the template descriptions now say so.

releases.headline: Restores Linux/macOS self-update, hardens sync recovery, config validation, and the support bundle
releases.summary: A correctness and security release. It restores in-daemon self-update on Linux and macOS, makes the Node.js version gate actually enforce its floor, stops a reconcile pass from overwriting a newer local edit with the server's older copy, ends several transfer-retry and reconnect loops, refuses a plaintext non-loopback server URL, closes support-bundle information leaks, and emits a schema-valid release SBOM. No configuration changes are required, though maxFileSize in config.json is now enforced.

items.title: In-daemon self-update installs again on Linux and macOS
items.body: The self-replace step now passes the verified SHA3-512 of the downloaded binary to the install call, which recently began requiring it. Without the hash the call was rejected before any file was touched, so a bare-binary daemon downloaded and verified an update but silently never installed it. Windows now also re-hashes the downloaded binary against the verified digest immediately before it replaces the running image.

items.title: The Node.js version gate now enforces the 24.18.0 floor
items.body: The startup check that refuses to run on an unsupported Node.js parsed the running version with a pattern that never matched the real version string, so it always fell through and enforced nothing. It now parses the version correctly and refuses to start below 24.18.0 with an actionable message. Prebuilt binaries embed a matching runtime and are unaffected.

items.title: A stranded local edit is no longer overwritten by the server's older copy
items.body: After an upload exhausted its retries, a later reconcile pass could re-download the server's older version over the newer local edit. The reconcile path now preserves the local bytes as a conflict copy first — the same protection the live-change paths already apply — so an edit that outran a failed upload is never lost.

items.title: Over-cap files and permanently-rejected transfers are no longer retried every cycle
items.body: A file larger than the effective per-file limit, or an upload the server permanently rejects, was re-attempted on every reconcile pass indefinitely. Such a transfer is now recorded once and skipped until a later success or a reconnect, ending the repeated wasted requests and error-log noise.

items.title: A stalled catch-up no longer reconnects in a loop
items.body: When a change at the top of a catch-up batch could not be applied (a locked or unreadable local file), the client could reconnect on every reconcile tick. It now reconnects to advance the cursor only when a pass actually recovered stranded data, so an unappliable change no longer drives an endless reconnect loop.

items.title: Bandwidth and concurrency limits above ~2 GB/s are no longer silently disabled
items.body: The upload/download rate limits and the upload-concurrency setting were coerced with a 32-bit truncation that wrapped a value at or above 2^31 to a negative number, silently disabling the limit or clamping concurrency to one. They now use the full integer range.

items.title: The support bundle no longer leaks the home-directory path or a credential
items.body: The diagnostic support bundle could include the absolute state-database path (revealing the OS user and home layout) and, in a free-form log line, a bearer credential. The path is now reduced to a basename, a bearer token is redacted by shape, and secret literals containing quotes or backslashes are matched in both their raw and JSON-escaped forms.

items.title: Config.json validation is stricter and clearer
items.body: A config.json whose top level is not an object, or whose server / bundle / share / folder fields are the wrong type, is now rejected at load with a message that names the real problem instead of failing opaquely later.

items.title: Plaintext http:// to a non-loopback server is refused
items.body: A plaintext http:// server URL disables TLS, mTLS, and the post-quantum group pinning, sending the API key and all traffic in the clear. It is now refused at config-load for any non-loopback host. A loopback target (a TLS-terminating sidecar on the same host, or a dev target) stays allowed; a deliberate non-loopback plaintext hop now requires HERMITSTASH_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=1.

items.title: maxFileSize in config.json is now enforced
items.body: The maxFileSize setting, previously accepted but ignored, now refuses a file larger than it before an upload or download begins. It can only lower the built-in per-file ceiling (HERMITSTASH_MAX_FILE_BYTES, default 256 GiB), never raise it. If you set a non-zero maxFileSize expecting it to have no effect, files above it will now be skipped with an actionable error.

items.title: The release SBOM is now a schema-valid CycloneDX 1.6 document
items.body: The generated CycloneDX SBOM placed externalReferences on a lifecycle entry, which the 1.6 schema forbids, so every release shipped a technically-invalid document. The references now sit on a valid component, so CycloneDX-aware scanners parse the SBOM cleanly.

items.title: The release and image pipelines pin their remaining tool downloads
items.body: The container-image build and code-scanning workflows now pin the vulnerability scanner and workflow linters to verified versions (with a checksum on the scanner binary) rather than a floating latest, and the image build checks out the exact commit its provenance names. This closes the gaps where a compromised upstream tool release could enter a privileged build step.

releases.headline: Refreshes the vendored framework and raises the Node.js floor to 24.18.0
releases.summary: A maintenance release. It refreshes the vendored cryptography and networking framework to its current release — picking up its hardening for WebSocket, HTTP, JSON, path, and regex handling — raises the minimum Node.js runtime to 24.18.0, and keeps the self-update flow working under the framework's stricter release-asset pattern check. No configuration changes are required.

items.title: Refreshed the vendored cryptography and networking framework
items.body: The vendored framework the client is built on was updated to its current release. The refresh brings its security hardening for the outbound WebSocket client, HTTP responses, size- and depth-capped JSON parsing, path-traversal-safe file resolution, and regular-expression safety — the primitives the client relies on when talking to a server.

items.title: Minimum Node.js runtime raised to 24.18.0
items.body: The runtime floor is now Node.js 24.18.0 (24.17.0 was a security release; 24.18.0 bundles SQLite 3.53.1 and a backup-path fix). Prebuilt binaries embed a matching runtime; only from-source installs need to act.

items.title: Self-update keeps working under the framework's stricter asset-pattern check
items.body: The framework now runs the release-asset match pattern through its ReDoS-safe regular-expression sanitizer. The pattern that selects this platform's binary and signature is now expressed as a bounded character class rather than an optional group with an inner quantifier — a shape the sanitizer refuses. Without this change the refreshed framework would have rejected the pattern and silently disabled self-update; stable, prerelease, and build-metadata release names all continue to match, and the wrong-platform and ML-DSA sidecar assets are still excluded.

items.title: Run Node.js 24.18.0 or newer for from-source installs
items.body: Upgrade the runtime to Node.js 24.18.0+ before running the client from a source checkout. Prebuilt binary releases embed their own runtime and need no action.

releases.headline: Extends the from-source startup integrity check to the framework's transitive bundles and emits strictly-valid SBOM package URLs
releases.summary: A supply-chain and startup-integrity release. The from-source startup check that verifies each vendored dependency against its recorded hash now also covers the framework's executable transitive bundles, which previously could execute before any check ran, and it refuses to start if the manifest has been stripped of everything to verify. The release SBOM now percent-encodes its Package URLs so a strict validator accepts them. Prebuilt binaries skip the startup check and are unaffected. No configuration changes are required.

items.title: The from-source startup integrity check now covers the framework's transitive bundles
items.body: Running the client from a source checkout verifies each vendored dependency file against the SHA-256 hashes recorded in the manifest, before the framework is loaded, and refuses to start on a mismatch. The check covered the framework's own files and two cryptographic bundles but not the other transitive bundles the framework executes at startup (elliptic-curve, PKI, and WebAuthn helpers) — a tampered one of those could have run before any check. Those bundles are now hashed by the same pre-load check, so a corrupted or tampered transitive bundle is refused first. Their hashes were already recorded for the SBOM; this puts them behind the gate. Prebuilt binaries skip this check and are unaffected.

items.title: Startup refuses to continue if the integrity manifest has nothing to verify
items.body: If the integrity manifest were stripped of its file and hash entries — a botched dependency refresh, a partial clone, or tampering — the startup check would previously verify zero files and pass silently. It now treats verifying nothing as a failure and refuses to start with an actionable message, so a manifest that lost its coverage is caught rather than waved through.

items.title: Release SBOM package URLs are percent-encoded
items.body: A component whose version string contained spaces or parentheses produced a Package URL (purl) with those characters left unencoded, which a strict purl validator rejects as malformed. Version components are now percent-encoded per the purl specification, so every component's purl in the release SBOM is syntactically valid. A normal semantic version is unchanged.
